new_issues.title: record_from_message accepts bool turns/cost_usd metadata because bool is an int.
new_issues.why: isinstance(turns, int) and isinstance(cost, float | int) do admit True. But the message metadata is written only by squadron's own providers (sdk/agent.py, openai/agent.py, codex/agent.py) from telemetry that read_result_usage already filters with _strict_int and a bool-rejecting cost check, so a bool cannot arrive. Speculative hardening.

new_issues.title: sq stats reviews derives the alias only from requestedModel, so standalone subscription reviews are labeled 'prov' instead of 'api-rate equiv.'.
new_issues.why: _record sets alias only when requestedModel is a known alias, but persistence writes requestedModel only when the model was substituted, and its value is the resolved model id, not the alias name; no other frontmatter key carries the alias. cost_cell labels a provider cost 'api-rate equiv.' only when record.alias has cost_tier subscription, so an SDK review on a subscription alias renders '$X prov', the notional-cost-as-money mislabel D3 exists to prevent. Same class as 175-I5, and still present in the moved reader at HEAD.

new_issues.title: sq stats reviews reads the reviews directory from the raw process cwd rather than the git root the review commands write under.
new_issues.why: stats_reviews uses Path.cwd() / REVIEWS_DIR while review commands anchor at resolve_repo_cwd (git root). Run from a subdirectory, it prints 'No review directory at <path>' rather than finding the artifacts. The inconsistency is true, but the result is an explicit message naming the path searched, not a silent empty report, and running from the repo root works; a usability point.

new_issues.title: The reviews table names only the first excluded pipeline run id.
new_issues.why: render_reviews_report prints the count and excluded[0] only; the JSON carries the full list. True, presentation-only, no wrong data.

new_issues.title: format_usd formats a negative sub-cent amount with two decimals.
new_issues.why: The guard is 0 < abs(amount) < 0.01, so -0.005 takes the four-decimal branch and renders '$-0.0050'; only magnitudes of a cent or more get two decimals, symmetrically for both signs. The claimed behavior does not occur.

new_issues.title: The partial-spend WARNING duplicates the session's stall warning.
new_issues.why: The session logs that the turn was silent and is being interrupted; record_from_telemetry logs a different fact, that the interrupted turn's spend is not recorded. That WARNING, with this exact text, is specified by slice design D5, so it is neither a duplicate of the same message nor an unintended polarity.
